angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,220,258 km at 35.09 pc = 0.46 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 7535: distance 35.088 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.034), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 35.088 +/- 1.193 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 30.3493 +/- 0.7237 mas (same row, RUWE 10.05), 41.9 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 1.754 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 7535: radius 1.754 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 5.565 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.066) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 1,220,258 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 6699 +/- 216 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 7535: effective temperature 6699 +/- 216 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.099) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 7535: effective temperature 6699 +/- 216 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.099) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
